{"self_assessment": "Impact: I laid the start domino and traced stroke 1, the top line of the fish body. That stroke carries the fall from the start to the nose and along the whole upper outline, so it is a large part of what the judge sees. It runs from the start across the top of the body to the tail loop. At the push, about 108 of the 111 standing dominoes were connected to the start, and the fish outline was complete.

Execution: I took stroke 1 as soon as the sketch was up and kept laying it in steady batches until it was finished. I then used close inspections on the nose and nearby stretches to check the chain, and stood a couple of dominoes back up when needed. In the last minutes I kept my hands off the finished build so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I confirmed the plan quickly and said which stroke I was on, so the others could start theirs without waiting. I left the nose joint to Hana once she had taken it, so two people weren't working in the same cramped spot. I kept the table updated in short messages and backed the hands-off agreement before the push.

Leadership: I committed to the fish idea without second-guessing it, took ownership of the stroke that carries the start, and stayed with it until it was done. I set an example of working quietly and steadily. I also held back from touching a finished build near the end, which kept the table calm and the fish intact.

Overall, I believe my work on the start and the top line was central to the result. The table's effort was shared, and I estimate my share at about 30%.", "my_share_percent": 30}
